## Natural history notes

A sleek swallow characterized by glossy blue-green upperparts, clean white underparts, long pointed wings, and a shallowly notched tail. In Florida, the Tree Swallow is mainly a winter visitor and migrant, found over marshes, lakes, ponds, wet prairies, coastal wetlands, fields, and open areas where flying insects are abundant. It feeds mostly by catching insects in flight, often gathering in large flocks, and also eats berries—especially wax myrtle and other small fruits—during cooler months when insects are less available.
